blocks.md: Although the revised observation interface produced accepted repairs on the isolated fixture in a later section, promoting that revision straight to full production traffic would expose live repositories and external services to unmeasured failure modes. That fixture result supports only testing the change on a broader task set; production authority is a separate grant.

blocks.title: Map of the section
blocks.md:
The section is organised as:

- Offline comparison and shadow evidence
- Canary task assignment
- Sequential monitoring
- Operational tripwires
- Release measurements

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Release gate matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A release decision is a declared conjunctive rule written before data and applied to an evidence record that keeps verdicts, paired cohorts, and diagnostics.

questions.q: The section **Staged Releases** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A release decision is a declared conjunctive rule written before data and applied to an evidence record that keeps verdicts, paired cohorts, and diagnostics.
Sampling may thin diagnostic detail but never the accounting record of admitted trials, verdicts, spend, and drops, and retention is chosen per verdict under storage and privacy budgets.
Release exposure is staged so each stage answers its own question (offline gate, shadow execution, bounded canary), with sequential monitoring and hard tripwires that stop admission.

Spans bind every model call, mediated tool execution, and check to their trial and artifact, but a diagnostic trace may sample or drop and never replaces the durable recovery log or the verdict record.
questions.hint: Re-read the excerpt and the section map: which idea is this section building toward?
questions.explanation: This section develops **Release gate**: A release decision is a declared conjunctive rule written before data and applied to an evidence record that keeps verdicts, paired cohorts, and diagnostics.
